title: Mohammad Aminul Haque's Groundbreaking Research Redefines Understanding of Islamic Bonds in Global Capital Markets
excerpt: Mohammad Aminul Haque, an internationally published researcher and finance scholar, has achieved a significant academic milestone with the publication of a high-impact research paper examining the fundamental differences between Islamic bonds (Sukuk) and conventional bonds in global capital markets.
content:
Mohammad Aminul Haque, an internationally published researcher and finance scholar, has achieved a significant academic milestone with the publication of a high-impact research paper examining the fundamental differences between Islamic bonds (Sukuk) and conventional bonds in global capital markets.

The research, titled "Are Islamic Bonds Different from Conventional Bonds? International Evidence from Capital Market Tests," was published in the prestigious Borsa Istanbul Review, a peer-reviewed journal published by Elsevier and indexed on ScienceDirect. The study is widely recognised for its rigorous empirical analysis and global relevance in the fields of finance, banking, and Islamic capital markets.

Co-authored by Mohammad Aminul Haque, the paper analyses 166 bond issuances across multiple international markets over nearly a decade, including periods before, during, and after the global financial crisis. The research provides rare, data-driven insights into how stock markets react differently to Sukuk and conventional bond announcements under varying economic conditions.

One of the study's key contributions is its evidence that Islamic bonds are perceived differently by financial markets, particularly during periods of financial stress. The findings challenge long-standing assumptions that Sukuk merely replicate conventional bonds, demonstrating instead that investor behaviour, risk perception, and wealth effects differ materially between the two instruments.

Industry experts and academics have highlighted the paper for its relevance to banks, policymakers, institutional investors, and regulators, especially as Islamic finance continues to grow globally as an alternative financing system. The research also contributes to resolving long-running debates on whether Islamic financial instruments offer genuine diversification and resilience advantages.

Mohammad Aminul Haque's publication strengthens his profile as a thought leader in Islamic finance, capital markets, and financial strategy, and underscores the growing global recognition of research emerging from international academic collaborations.

The full research paper is available on ScienceDirect and continues to be cited by scholars and practitioners worldwide, reinforcing its lasting impact on global financial research.

Reference: Nafis Alam, M. Kabir Hassan, Mohammad Aminul Haque, 'Are Islamic bonds different from conventional bonds? International evidence from capital market tests', Science Direct, Volume 13, Issue 3, Sep 2013 (one of Highest cited publications in Islamic Bond).

title: LankaBangla Finance and Nagad Sign Strategic Deal
excerpt: LankaBangla Finance and Nagad signed a strategic partnership deal, facilitated by Mohammad Aminul Haque's leadership.
content:
A corporate agreement was signed between LankaBangla Finance Limited and Nagad, the digital financial arm of the Bangladesh Post Office, in November 2020. Khwaja Shahriar, Managing Director and CEO of LankaBangla Finance Limited, and Mohammad Aminul Haque, Director, CEO (Acting) and CFO of Nagad, signed the agreement on behalf of their respective organisations.

Under this agreement, LankaBangla Finance Limited customers will be able to enjoy convenient facilities for their credit card bill payment, monthly deposit and loan instalment payment through Nagad from anywhere across Bangladesh at any time without any hassle.

Driving towards new innovations and digitization, LankaBangla Finance Limited is always one step ahead in providing better services to its customers through advanced technology. The company is trying to bring more customers under its service umbrella by providing easy and secure financial services across the country.

Nagad, the fastest growing digital financial service of the country, already secured its position as second largest mobile financial service carrier of Bangladesh, a thriving provider that introduces several state of the art technologies in this field only in its one and half years' journey. The state owned carrier Nagad, also became the ultimate choice of the users because of its convenience and the low-cost service.

With this corporate agreement both LankaBangla Finance Limited and Nagad can bring about a change and add value to the lifestyle of customers.
